Work in C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (a Next.js 16 + Prisma app called Kodely — an AI website builder).

BUILD: the foundation of an asset library that generated sites can use.

## Read this constraint FIRST — it defines the whole design
Kodely's generated sites are Vite+React+TS+Tailwind apps compiled server-side and served under a STRICT CSP that blocks every external host. Read lib/agent.ts's SYSTEM prompt and lib/foundation.ts to see this. Concretely:
- NO remote images, NO CDN, NO Google Fonts, NO external anything. They fail silently at serve time.
- The only image mechanisms that work are: inline SVG, CSS gradients, and data: URIs.
- The generated project cannot add npm dependencies.

So an "asset library" here CANNOT be a stock-photo API. It must be assets that can be inlined into the generated source. That is the honest fit, and it is what you should build. If you think some category can't work under these constraints, say so in your report rather than shipping something that silently breaks.

## Scope — YOU MAY ONLY CREATE/EDIT FILES UNDER `lib/assets/` and `app/api/assets/`
Everything else is off limits — other agents are working in parallel. Read anything you need.

## What to build
1. **A curated inline-SVG icon set** (`lib/assets/icons.ts` or similar) — a genuinely useful set (60-120 icons) covering what small-business sites actually need: contact (phone, mail, map pin, clock), social (instagram, facebook, x, linkedin, tiktok, youtube, whatsapp), commerce (cart, card, tag, truck), food (coffee, utensils, pizza, wine), services (scissors, dumbbell, wrench, paw, camera, brush), UI (check, arrow, chevron, menu, close, star, quote, play). Each as a clean 24x24 stroke SVG path string with a stable id and searchable keywords. Multiple weights/styles if you can do it cheaply, but breadth of coverage matters more than style variety.

2. **Country flags** (`lib/assets/flags.ts`) — as compact inline SVG or CSS. Be pragmatic: a full 250-country set of accurate SVG flags is too much to hand-author. Do whichever of these you can genuinely deliver and be explicit about which you chose: (a) a subset of the most-requested ~40 countries as real SVG, (b) all countries as emoji flag glyphs (which are text, work everywhere, and need no assets at all), or (c) both, with emoji as the fallback. Do not fabricate a "complete" set that is actually wrong.

3. **Generated/procedural assets** (`lib/assets/patterns.ts`) — things that are pure CSS or generated SVG and therefore cost nothing: gradient presets (named, tasteful, a real palette not random hues), mesh/blob backgrounds, noise/grain overlays, section divider shapes (wave, angle, curve), dot/grid/stripe patterns, and simple avatar placeholders (initials-on-generated-colour, deterministic from a name).

4. **A search index + query function** (`lib/assets/index.ts`) — `findAssets(query, {kind, limit})` doing keyword/synonym matching over everything above, returning stable ids plus the inlinable source. This is the seam a future agent tool calls; design the signature for that even though wiring it into the agent prompt is NOT your job.

5. **An API route** `app/api/assets/route.ts` — GET with a `q` param returning matches as JSON. Auth-gate it the way other routes under app/api do (read one first — most use `requireUser().catch(() => null)`). This is for a future asset-picker UI.

## Critical constraints
- DO NOT modify: prisma/schema.prisma, lib/credits.ts, lib/agent.ts, lib/agent-sdk.ts, lib/build-site.ts, lib/events.ts, lib/build-narration.ts, lib/foundation.ts, app/api/generate/route.ts, app/projects/[id]/Editor.tsx, app/globals.css, proxy.ts, deploy.sh, .env, package.json, app/settings/**, app/dashboard/**.
- DO NOT add npm dependencies. No icon packages — hand-author or generate the SVG path data.
- DO NOT run `npm run build`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `deploy.sh`.
- Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint <your files>` and make sure YOUR files are clean. Other files may have pre-existing errors — ignore those, they are not yours.
- Licensing matters: everything must be your own hand-authored geometry or genuinely public-domain/CC0. Do NOT copy path data out of a licensed icon set (Font Awesome Pro, Noun Project, etc.). Say in your report what the provenance of your icon geometry is.
- Keep the total module size sane — this gets imported server-side. Note the byte size in your report.

## Report back
What you built, which flag approach you chose and why, the provenance of the icon geometry, total module size, what you verified, and which asset categories from the brief you concluded are impossible under the CSP constraint.

 * Generated sites are served under a CSP of

function buildBody(def: IconDef): string {
  const paths = def.d ? def.d.split("|").map((d) => `<path d="${d}"/>`).join("") : "";
  return paths + (def.b ?? "");
}

function keywordsFor(def: IconDef): string[] {
  const fromId = def.id.split("-");
  const fromName = def.name.toLowerCase().split(/[^a-z0-9]+/).filter(Boolean);
  return Array.from(new Set([...fromId, ...fromName, ...def.k.split(" "), def.c]));
}

export const ICONS: Icon[] = DEFS.map((def) => ({
  id: def.id,
  name: def.name,
  category: def.c,
  keywords: keywordsFor(def),
  body: buildBody(def),
}));

const BY_ID = new Map(ICONS.map((icon) => [icon.id, icon]));

export function getIcon(id: string): Icon | undefined {
  return BY_ID.get(id);
}

export type IconRenderOptions = {
  /** Pixel size for width/height. Omit to emit a size-less svg sized by CSS. */
  size?: number | null;
  /** A named weight, or an explicit stroke width. Default "regular" (1.75). */
  weight?: IconWeight | number;
  /** Added to the root <svg>. */
  className?: string;
  /** Stroke colour. Defaults to currentColor so the icon inherits text colour. */
  color?: string;
  /**
   * Accessible name. When omitted the icon is emitted as aria-hidden, which is
   * the right default for an icon sitting next to a text label.
   */
  title?: string;
};

function strokeWidthOf(weight: IconRenderOptions["weight"]): number {
  if (typeof weight === "number") return weight;
  return ICON_WEIGHTS[weight ?? "regular"];
}

/**
 * A standalone `<svg>` string — paste into HTML, or into JSX after running it
 * through {@link iconJsx}.
 */
export function iconSvg(id: string, opts: IconRenderOptions = {}): string | null {
  const icon = BY_ID.get(id);
  if (!icon) return null;
  const { size = 24, className, color = "currentColor", title } = opts;
  const dims = size == null ? "" : ` width="${size}" height="${size}"`;
  const cls = className ? ` class="${className}"` : "";
  const label = title
    ? ` role="img" aria-label="${title.replace(/"/g, """)}"`
    : ` aria-hidden="true"`;
  return (
    `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="${ICON_VIEWBOX}"${dims}` +
    ` fill="none" stroke="${color}" stroke-width="${strokeWidthOf(opts.weight)}"` +
    ` stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"${cls}${label}>${icon.body}</svg>`
  );
}

// The only kebab-case SVG attributes this module ever emits. Rewriting exactly
// these (rather than every hyphenated token) keeps path data untouched.
const JSX_ATTRS: [RegExp, string][] = [
  [/\bstroke-width=/g, "strokeWidth="],
  [/\bstroke-linecap=/g, "strokeLinecap="],
  [/\bstroke-linejoin=/g, "strokeLinejoin="],
  [/\bfill-rule=/g, "fillRule="],
  [/\bclip-rule=/g, "clipRule="],
  [/\bstop-color=/g, "stopColor="],
  [/\baria-hidden=/g, "aria-hidden="],
  [/\bclass=/g, "className="],
];

/** The same markup with JSX-safe attribute names — ready to drop into a .tsx file. */
export function toJsx(svg: string): string {
  return JSX_ATTRS.reduce((acc, [re, to]) => acc.replace(re, to), svg);
}

export function iconJsx(id: string, opts: IconRenderOptions = {}): string | null {
  const svg = iconSvg(id, opts);
  return svg === null ? null : toJsx(svg);
}

/**
 * `data:` URI form, for CSS `background-image` / `<img src>`. Allowed by the
 * sandbox CSP (`img-src 'self' data:`). Note that `currentColor` does NOT
 * resolve inside a data URI — pass an explicit `color`.
 */
export function iconDataUri(id: string, opts: IconRenderOptions = {}): string | null {
  const svg = iconSvg(id, { color: "#000000", ...opts });
  if (svg === null) return null;
  return `data:image/svg+xml,${encodeURIComponent(svg).replace(/'/g, "%27")}`;
}

/** All categories present, in declaration order, with their icon counts. */
export function iconCategories(): { category: IconCategory; count: number }[] {
  const counts = new Map<IconCategory, number>();
  for (const icon of ICONS) counts.set(icon.category, (counts.get(icon.category) ?? 0) + 1);
  return Array.from(counts, ([category, count]) => ({ category, count }));
}

content.text:
Cleaned up the scratch servers. Everything is verified.

## What I built

Five new files, all inside the allowed scope (`lib/assets/**`, `app/api/assets/**`). Nothing else was touched.

**`lib/assets/icons.ts`** — 147 icons on a 24×24 grid across 9 categories (contact 10, social 10, commerce 12, food 12, services 21, people 6, media 17, nature 8, UI 51). Three weights (`light`/`regular`/`bold`) come from a render-time `stroke-width` over one geometry, so styles cost zero extra bytes. Renderers: `iconSvg`, `iconJsx` (kebab→camel attribute rewrite), `iconDataUri`.

**`lib/assets/flags.ts`** — **I chose (c), both.** All 250 ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 countries (+EU) resolve to a flag emoji computed arithmetically from the two letters — no lookup table, complete by construction, and it's *text*, so it needs no asset at all. On top of that, 55 hand-authored SVG flags, each tagged `accuracy: "exact" | "simplified"` with a `note` naming exactly what's approximated. 42 are exact (band flags, Nordic crosses, Greece, Japan, India's 24-spoke chakra, the US 50-star grid, Turkey's crescent, South Africa's Y); 13 are explicitly simplified (UK's diagonal counterchange isn't reproduced; Brazil's stars/motto, Argentina's sun face, Spain's and Portugal's arms omitted; Canada's leaf is a hand-authored 11-point approximation). **Countries whose flags are mostly a detailed emblem — Mexico, Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka, Bhutan — are deliberately absent from the SVG layer rather than shipped wrong.** They fall through to emoji. One honest caveat documented in the module: Windows Chrome/Edge render regional-indicator pairs as two grey letter boxes, so emoji flags are right for pickers and phone-code lists, not for a design leaning on the flag as an image.

**`lib/assets/patterns.ts`** — 30 named gradients (curated palette across warm/cool/vivid/nature/neutral/pastel/dark, each with a Tailwind arbitrary-value class), 6 mesh backgrounds, 3 feTurbulence grain textures as `data:` URIs, 12 section dividers on a stretched 1440×120 canvas with flip options, 12 pure-CSS repeating patterns, and deterministic initials avatars (FNV-1a → hue, so the same person gets the same colour every rebuild).

**`lib/assets/index.ts`** — `findAssets(query, {kind, limit, weight})` over all 461 entries with AND-ish multi-token scoring and a query-side synonym map covering trade vocabulary (`plumber`→wrench, `dentist`→tooth) and British spellings. Every match carries a paste-ready `source` plus a one-line `usage`. Also `getAsset`, `listAssets`, `listAssetIds`, `assetCatalogSummary`. Designed as the seam a future `search_assets` agent tool forwards straight through.

## Provenance

All icon geometry is hand-authored from primitives (lines, circles, rounded rects, single arcs), with corner rounding delegated to `stroke-linejoin="round"` rather than drawn. No path data was copied from any icon library, free or licensed. The social marks are simplified generic renderings from the same primitives — not the trademark artwork; I noted in the module that commercial use should check each platform's brand guidelines. Flag geometry is generated from arithmetic in the file or authored from published construction specifications.

107 KB of source (icons 38.8, flags 26.3, patterns 22.7, index 16.5, route 3.0). Materialising the *entire* catalogue at once produces ~277 KB of strings, but that only happens on an unfiltered `listAssets()`; the API caps at 100 results and defaults to 24.

## Verified

`npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint` both clean on my files. I rendered all 147 icons, all 55 flags, and every gradient/mesh/texture/pattern/divider/avatar into a browser and inspected them visually. Two real bugs found and fixed that way:

- `handshake` rendered as an unreadable knot — replaced with `bed` (hotels/B&Bs were an actual gap; "partnership" is served by `users`).
- `plus-grid` rendered blank — its CSS mask was misaligned, and worse, `mask-image` on a section would have clipped the section's own text. Replaced with `dots-offset`, which gets the same feel from backgrounds alone.

Also caught that `dividerSvg` emitted an inline `style` attribute, which is a string in HTML but must be an object in JSX — it would have broken on paste into a `.tsx`. Switched to `class="block w-full"`, which `toJsx` converts correctly. Flags, dividers and avatars now emit JSX in `source` with raw SVG in `variants`.

## What is impossible under the CSP — and one thing the prompt currently gets away with

- **Stock photography / any raster imagery.** No remote host, and a base64 hero JPEG would have to pass verbatim through `write_file` — that's 150–400 KB of tokens per image. Not viable. The initials avatars are the honest stand-in for headshots.
- **Icon fonts, CDN sprite sheets, Lottie/animation libraries.** No external hosts, no new npm deps.
- **Custom web fonts — including base64 ones.** This one is worth flagging: the CSP is `default-src 'self'; ... img-src 'self' data:`. `img-src` names `data:` explicitly, but there is **no `font-src`**, so it falls back to `default-src 'self'` — which does *not* include `data:`. A `@font-face` with a base64 `src` is therefore blocked, not just a Google Fonts `<link>`. A self-hosted `.woff2` would satisfy `'self'` but can't be produced, since project files are stored as text. The system font stack is genuinely the only option, which is what `lib/agent.ts` already instructs — the prompt's advice is correct, but for a stricter reason than the "no @import or `<link>`" wording implies. Might be worth tightening that line if someone later relaxes the CSP.
- **Accurate flags for emblem-heavy countries.** Not impossible in principle, but not honestly hand-authorable at quality — hence the emoji fallback and the explicit `accuracy` field instead of a fake "complete set".
